bookingsBacklog.title: New contracts (Bookings) and order backlog
bookingsBacklog.content:
Bookings is the value of new signalling/communication contracts CRSC won in the period (tendered by state railway and metro authorities); backlog is the stock of signed-but-unrecognised contract value still to be converted into revenue as projects are delivered. Both are annual-only disclosures.

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): this is the single most important forward indicator for the bear case — new contracts fell from RMB70.6bn (FY2019) to RMB44.1bn (FY2025, -11.8% YoY), and backlog has followed, down from RMB122.9bn (FY2024) to RMB115.9bn (FY2025). Because backlog converts to revenue over several years, today's bookings shortfall shows up as revenue pressure a year or more out, not immediately.

What to watch:

  • Whether bookings stabilise or keep falling as China's rail/metro capex cycle matures
  • Backlog-to-revenue ratio (cover) shrinking, which signals a thinner forward revenue runway
  • H1-only bookings prints (no backlog disclosed at half-year) as an early read before the full-year number

rd.title: Research & development spend
rd.content:
R&D expense is cash and expensed cost spent developing new signalling, train-control and communication technology; shown here against revenue to track R&D intensity.

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): R&D has kept rising even as bookings and backlog have fallen (RMB1.05bn FY2016 to RMB2.01bn FY2025) — management is sustaining technology investment (e.g. higher-speed and autonomous train-control systems) through the order-book downturn rather than cutting it, which pressures margins if the top line does not recover.

What to watch:

  • R&D % of revenue rising while bookings fall (spending discipline under pressure)
  • Whether R&D is translating into new contract wins or export orders that could offset the domestic slowdown

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
